zh.title: 空中巴士預測2045年航空業人力需求達244萬人
zh.summary: 空中巴士預測，航空業至2045年將需要244萬名工作人員。
body: 空中巴士在10月14日發布的《全球服務市場預測》中估計，全球航空業到2045年將需要244萬名工作人員。預測列出的需求包括66萬名飛行員、73萬名維修技術人員，以及105萬名客艙組員。
空中巴士並預期，屆時全球每年航空旅客人次將達100億，全球機隊規模將增至45,550架。該公司預測，航空訓練市場到2045年每年將達170億美元。
空中巴士表示，業界若要滿足預測的人力需求，需加強招募與訓練。這項預測涵蓋各製造商的飛機，聚焦於座位數超過100的客機，以及載貨能力超過22,000磅的貨機。

en.title: Airbus forecasts aviation industry will need 2.44 million workers by 2045
en.summary: Airbus forecasts 2.44 million aviation workers will be needed by 2045.
body: In its Global Services Forecast released on October 14, Airbus estimates the global aviation industry will need 2.44 million workers by 2045. The projected requirement includes 660,000 pilots, 730,000 maintenance technicians and 1.05 million cabin crew.

Airbus also expects annual passenger numbers to reach 10 billion and the global aircraft fleet to grow to 45,550 over that period. It forecasts that the aviation training market will reach $17 billion annually by 2045.

Airbus said meeting the projected staffing needs will require the industry to step up recruitment and training. The forecast covers aircraft from all manufacturers, focusing on passenger jets with more than 100 seats and freighters capable of carrying more than 22,000 pounds.

zh.title: FAA恢復空中交通管制員飛行甲板訓練計畫
zh.summary: FAA恢復管制員飛行甲板訓練，正式計畫預計感恩節後啟動。
body: 美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）宣佈恢復「Flight Deck Training」計畫，讓空中交通管制員可申請搭乘符合資格航班，親身瞭解飛行甲板作業。
管制員每年可參與兩班商業或一般航空航班，以及一班軍用航班。FAA表示，美國主要航空公司均已同意參與。
FAA表示，測試已發現計畫效益，包括協助管制員判斷何時應避免發布複雜指令，並瞭解更改降落跑道等指令對飛行員工作量的影響。正式計畫預計感恩節後啟動。

en.title: FAA Reinstates Flight Deck Training Program for Air Traffic Controllers
en.summary: FAA reinstates controller flight deck training; formal program expected after Thanksgiving.
body: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced the reinstatement of its Flight Deck Training program for air traffic controllers. The program lets controllers apply for jumpseat access on eligible flights to gain firsthand experience with flight deck operations.
Controllers may take part in two commercial or general aviation flights and one military flight per year. The FAA says all major U.S. airlines have agreed to participate.

The FAA says testing has identified benefits, including helping controllers recognize when to avoid complex instructions and understand how instructions such as landing-runway changes can affect pilot workload. The formal program is expected to begin after Thanksgiving.
